chapter: Cab Calloway, Haiti and Sarah Vaughan
title: Five years teaching in Haiti, the Billy Taylor Quartet and Marian Anderson
summary: Budd returns to Haiti yearly, brings the Billy Taylor quartet to the centennial fair, and plays for a colonel at the palace.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So anyway, I went down to Haiti from then for about five straight years; every year I used to go down there and teach. My first stint was three months. The next time I went down to Haiti, they were having their centennial down there from all of the islands, and I took the Billy Taylor

quartet with me and went down there. And we played in concert, and on the concert -- the fair -- with Marian Anderson, and we had, you know, the reception from the Haitian government with Marian Anderson, and we were all there.
Did you ever get to know the great Haitian Fenlan, a great writer?

I knew of him. I didn't know him personally. Yes, I knew of him. He was a great writer. I met a lot of great men there. I met many Senators and Congressmen, and I knew at the time that I went there, Estimee was president, and he was responsible for the world's fair down there. They claimed that he absconded, but like -- oh, they put him in exile, because they said that he got so much money. Well, this happens in everything. But anyway, under him was Paul E. [crossed out] His last name sounds like this MA-GWAR. He was a colonel of the armies, and he thought I was a great man, and he used to send his private car to get me to come to the palace and play for the soldiers.
